output.normalized_title: redis-cluster: Write latency spiked to 4200ms on primary-db (redis-cluster)
symptoms: Write latency spiked to 4200ms on primary-db

output.classification_reasoning: The incident involves a Redis cluster where write latency on the primary database node spiked dramatically (4200 ms) and secondary telemetry also showed anomalies. This points to a degradation in the data store's performance rather than a network, authentication, or storage capacity issue. The latency spike affects a large user base (3,500 users) and persisted for over an hour, indicating a non‑trivial but contained problem within the database layer. The root cause likely involves internal Redis clustering mechanics, replication lag, or resource contention, which typically requires multi‑step investigation (e.g., examining node health, memory pressure, and cluster rebalancing). Hence, the failure is classified as a database_problem with a Moderate operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Do not terminate primary node without promoting a read‑replica first. Verify that writes are frozen (write‑freeze) before any restart or reboot of the primary database instance.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: Write latency spiked to 4200ms on primary-db

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Current telemetry matches the Write latency spike pattern observed in INC-1010 (payment-processor). The recurring error signature ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 and identical symptom suggest a common underlying database latency issue affecting multiple services.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident affects 3,500 users, far exceeding the 2,000‑user cross‑tier threshold defined in the SLA rule. Although the service tier is Tier‑2, the rule applies when the aggregate user impact across tiers reaches 2,000 or more. The outage duration of 79 minutes is significant but does not alone trigger a higher severity; the primary determinant is the user count. The deterministic rule therefore mandates SEV‑2. The confirmed root cause (database write latency) aligns with the recurring pattern from INC‑1010, reinforcing the impact assessment. Consequently, the final severity level is SEV‑2.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has root or ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production us-east-1 cluster.
verification: AWS identity shows role ProdOperations
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1

remediation_steps.title: Freeze Writes and Verify Write‑Freeze
remediation_steps.description: Activate the write‑freeze flag on the primary database to stop new write traffic while remediation proceeds.
verification: Parameter group includes write-freeze flag
No new write transactions observed in telemetry for 30 seconds

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Promote the healthiest read‑replica to become the new primary to restore low‑latency writes.
verification: Replica status changes to 'available' and role = 'primary'
Write latency metric drops below 200ms for 5 consecutive minutes

remediation_steps.title: Re‑attach Application Endpoints to New Primary
remediation_steps.description: Update Kubernetes ConfigMaps/Secrets that point services (redis‑cluster, payment‑processor) to the new primary endpoint.
commands: kubectl set env deployment/redis-cluster PRIMARY_DB_ENDPOINT=$(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier replica-db-01 --query 'DBInstances[0].Endpoint.Address' --output text)
kubectl set env deployment/payment-processor PRIMARY_DB_ENDPOINT=$(aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier replica-db-01 --query 'DBInstances[0].Endpoint.Address' --output text)
verification: Pods restart and reach READY state
Application logs show successful DB connection to new endpoint

remediation_steps.title: Unfreeze Writes and Monitor
remediation_steps.description: Remove the write‑freeze flag and monitor latency and error rates to confirm stability.
commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name WriteLatency --dimensions Name=DBInstanceIdentifier,Value=replica-db-01 --statistics Average --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-5 minutes' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: Write‑freeze flag removed
Write latency remains <200ms for 10 minutes
ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 count drops to zero

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks against affected services and confirm no residual errors.
verification: Both health endpoints return HTTP 200 with status OK
No recent ERR_DATABASE_PROBLEM_611 entries in logs

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: If any step fails or latency remains elevated, revert to the original primary-db instance and restore previous service endpoint configurations. All changes are reversible via RDS read‑replica promotion rollback and Kubernetes rollout undo.

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica and re‑enable the original primary as writer.
verification: Primary-db status = 'available' and role = 'primary'
Write latency on primary-db returns to pre‑remediation levels

steps.description: Rollback Kubernetes environment variables to point back to original primary.
verification: Pods restart and report connection to primary-db
No connection errors in pod logs

steps.description: Remove write‑freeze flag if still present.
verification: Parameter group no longer includes write-freeze

commands: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name WriteLatency --statistics Average --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-5 minutes' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: Health endpoints return OK
Write latency on primary-db is within acceptable SLA (<500ms)

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified (root or ProdOperations SSO)
Current backup snapshot of primary-db exists and is recent
